utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-99-36-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal versus Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Appearances for the Prosecution, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is James Stewart. I am appearing on behalf of the Prosecutor with co-counsel, Mr. Michael Keegan, with legal officer, Ann Sutherland, and case manager, Adele Erasmus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Vladimir Petrovic. I am defence counsel from Belgrade. The Registry of the Tribunal has asked me to act as defence counsel for Mr. Talic at this initial appearance. I work for the Fila Law Office in Belgrade. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have you had the opportunity of discussing this indictment with your client, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yesterday, I visited Mr. Talic at the detention unit of the United Nations, and we looked into all the legal and factual aspects of the indictment, and I believe that Mr. Talic today is in a position to state his position as regards the charges brought against him in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that he understands the nature of the charges against him?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that he fully understands the nature of the charges brought against him and that he can make his plea. I think that he fully understands the indictment and that there will be no problems whatsoever in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Talic, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I can, and I fully understand the entire dialogue that has been carried on so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give us your full name? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Momir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Momir Talic? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] "Talic" is my last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the date upon which you believe you were born? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] The 15th of July, 1942.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your address was, your residence, before you were arrested? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] The Hotel Sico, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Petrovic, it's common practice within this Tribunal for the accused to waive his right to have the indictment read out in full before entering a plea. Have you had the opportunity of discussing that with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had an opportunity of discussing this with Mr. Talic. I presented both options to him. Mr. Talic read the entire indictment in the Serbian language several times, and together we reached the conclusion that it was not necessary to have the indictment read in its entirety before this Court but only the actual count that is brought against Mr. Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Talic, stand up, if you would, please. The charge against you is that you committed persecutions on political, racial, or religious grounds, a crime against humanity. I'm now going to ask you to plead to that charge. Your response should be "guilty" or "not guilty," as the case may be. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. The Registrar will be instructed to set a date for trial, subject to any further order of the Trial Chamber. Are there any other matters that can be dealt with at this stage? Yes, Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There are just two matters. First of all, I would like to inform the Chamber that we are in a position to make immediate Rule 47 supporting material disclosure in both English and B/C/S once permanent counsel is appointed for the accused. Secondly, I'll simply state for the record that this accused is jointly charged with Radoslav Brdjanin, and we have filed a document reflecting this in accordance with certain orders made by the confirming judge in March of this year, and in due course, that document, that indictment will be conveyed to the Defence. We've filed it with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You've got it in the Bosnian Serbo-Croatian language as well, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We have it in English at this stage, and it will be rendered into French and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The Rule 72 application, if there be one, will no doubt depend upon the date of your filing or serving the one in the language which the accused understands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We appreciate that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you got anything that you want to raise, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would just like to correct the translation that we heard in the Serbian language. It said that General Talic was condemned. He was not condemned. He was indicted. That is the only thing I wish to mention, in addition to one more thing. I was asked by the Registry to appear at this initial appearance. Together with Mr. Keegan, I discussed this matter, and I had to inform him that I could not take over this material because Mr. Talic has not made his final decision yet as to who he's going to entrust with his defence. Therefore, I believe that the supporting materials should remain pending until the final decision is made by Mr. Talic, that is, who is going to be his defence counsel in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I understand. You have, no doubt, advised him that he should make up his mind as soon as possible about obtaining legal representation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what the Registry of the Tribunal did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your assistance. We will adjourn.
